narrative: Material PL1__M3813B21 exhibits erratic demand (CV=0.54) with a mean of 278.19 units/day and 93.1% non-zero days, indicating an active but volatile consumption pattern requiring robust buffering. Lead times average 4.07 days with moderate variability (CV=0.376) after removing two data-entry outliers of over 9,000 days. The recommended (r,Q) continuous-review policy sets safety stock at 859 units and an order quantity of 2,009 units, achieving the 95% service-level target while fully respecting the 2,869-unit storage capacity constraint. Transitioning from the current SAP policy of zero safety stock and MOQ-sized orders reduces annual total cost by 90.5% (from $86,210 to $8,179) by consolidating ~861 micro-orders into approximately 36 economic replenishments per year.

research_insights.selected_model: EOQ with safety stock (r,Q) continuous-review policy, Normal approximation z=1.645
research_insights.selection_rationale: Selected EOQ model due to erratic demand pattern with 93% non-zero demand days. The (r,Q) continuous-review framework is appropriate for materials with predominantly non-zero daily consumption. Normal approximation is justified given 130 observations and a CV of 0.54 that does not indicate extreme intermittency.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Medium risk: EOQ of 2,427 units was capped to 2,009 units due to storage constraint of 2,869 units minus 859 safety stock = 2,010 available. The capacity constraint binds and reduces order quantity by ~17%, slightly increasing ordering frequency and cost versus the unconstrained optimum. Lead-time CV of 0.376 triggers a 1.05x disruption premium.
